name: manual_e390f2
claim: A documented cross-repo sync policy (orama-system's scripts/git/* are canonical; PT's copies must be byte-identical downstream mirrors, never hand-edited, per AGENTS.md in both repos) can still be silently violated even while fully documented, if a fix gets made directly in the downstream repo during a work session and the sync-back step is skipped or forgotten. The policy being written down is necessary but not sufficient -- periodically diff the actual file contents across repos (not just trust that "the policy says X, so X is true") to catch drift before it compounds. When drift is found, verify which side is actually more advanced by reading the diffs, not by assuming the documented-canonical side is automatically correct -- the downstream repo can genuinely be ahead if fixes landed there first.

decisions.notes: A documented cross-repo policy was still silently violated this session -- worth recording that documentation alone doesn't prevent drift, only periodic verification does.

rationale: A documented cross-repo policy was still silently violated this session -- worth recording that documentation alone doesn't prevent drift, only periodic verification does.
